correctness.rationale: Read actual KIT full-paper equations (3.16), (4.1), their coefficients Gamma and Lemma 4.1 small-tau conditions; the scalar reduction uses mass 1/6 and stiffness 4, normalized eigenvalue 24, alpha=1/12,beta=1/72. The second iterate factorizes as -(x^3+x-a)(x^2-a*x+1)/((1+x^2)^2+a^2), verified independently with SymPy. This gives global half-line convergence for a<=2 and exactly one attracting primitive 2-cycle for a>2, with p q=1, p+q=a and 4/a^2 derivative product. Not a challenge to a theorem that requires small enough tau.
